type: membership by reference: a layer is a named header-table record holding a section-1 pointer word to the placement record; the rule excludes the placement's own blob, records of the placement class itself, and records named by an .ai or .mdl path
structure: Which named groups a placement belongs to, resolved without a runtime fixup map

location.offset: e.g. the tutorial placement 0x189088 is referenced by 0x3E4C10 inside the record 0x3E4BCC named "HatBoxPickup.lvl" and by 0x189084 inside 0x186EFC named ".../Hat_Pickup.ai" (the script, excluded); layer names seen include Plants, Loot, OpeningCS, Mabu_Citizens, Level_027_plants.lvl

meaning: Layers are the natural object list of an editor and were previously only obtainable from a runtime fixup map, which costs two boots per level. Reading them structurally needs a reverse index over the object section, but a raw index is not usable on its own: of the 2 123 words that resolve to a placement in the tutorial only 68.3% are words the game actually rewrote. The rule above makes it exact. Measured against the tutorial's runtime fixup map, the 1 170 words it keeps are runtime pointers at 100.00%, and it reproduces every layer label the fixup-based implementation reported (1 077 of 1 077) while recovering 93 further referrers that implementation had dropped through a hardcoded class whitelist (classes 83, 151, 68 and 160). Applied to five IGZ files, 97.6% to 100% of placements carry at least one layer. Still LIKELY rather than CONFIRMED: the rule is validated against a runtime map on one level, not by a boot that depends on it.

evidence.probe: scratch layers2.mjs / layers3.mjs: structural reverse index over section 1 compared label by label with the layers derived from the runtime fixup map (ptr-scan3)
evidence.summary: recall 1077/1077 layer labels; the variant that also excludes referrers of the placement class itself cuts the extra labels from 333 to 75 and raises exact set matches from 409 to 595 of 664

evidence.summary: 1170 of 1170 kept words are in the runtime fixup map (100.00%); all 75 extra labels come from runtime pointer words whose owning class the previous whitelist excluded, so they are recovered referrers rather than false positives
